abstract: Sex pheromones are environmentally friendly alternatives to traditional insecticides for pest control. The high synthesis cost, however, has restricted large-scale application. Plant-based biofactories provide a promising, sustainable route for cost-effective production that could facilitate the broader use of pheromone-based pest control. Mating disruption of the yellow peach moth, Conogethes punctiferalis--a serious pest of fruit trees and field crops in East Asia--can be achieved using (E)-10-hexadecenal and (Z)-10-hexadecenal, two components of its sex pheromone. To enable rational reconstruction of the biosynthetic pathway towards these unusual fatty acid derivatives in heterologous production systems, we first elucidated their biosynthesis by combining in vivo labeling experiments, transcriptomics and functional characterization of candidate desaturase and reductase genes using Nicotiana benthamiana and yeast expression systems. We identified a rare {Delta}10 fatty acyl desaturase that catalyzes the production of both (E)-10- and (Z)-10-hexadecenoic acids, along with a downstream fatty acyl reductase with higher activity on the E isomer. We further introduced this {Delta}10 desaturase together with an acyl-ACP thioesterase-1 into Camelina sativa to redirect seed lipid metabolism towards the accumulation of the pheromone precursor fatty acids. After four generations of selection, we obtained stably inherited Camelina lines accumulating up to 4.7% of target fatty acids in total seed lipids, with individual seeds containing up to 8.3 g, without significant effects on plant growth or seed viability. These findings demonstrate how elucidating moth pheromone biosynthetic pathways can support the development of sustainable biotechnological production systems for pheromone-based pest management.

metadata.title: Reconstruction of a rare {triangleup}10 desaturation pathway enables production of yellow peach moth pheromone precursors in Camelina sativa

summary: Elucidates a rare Δ10 desaturase-reductase pathway for yellow peach moth pheromone precursors and engineers Camelina sativa seeds to accumulate them.
title: Reconstruction of a rare {triangleup}10 desaturation pathway enables production of yellow peach moth pheromone precursors in Camelina sativa
